relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with sporadic Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "genetic laboratory testing reported a mutation in NOD2/CARD15 (R334Q) gene".
method_note: Read in full by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from hand-chosen values and spans. One in-scope patient (label 'patient', rule 5) plus her two parents, who were tested and did not carry the variant ('This mutation was not found in her parents'); parents' sex not stated, so labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'. Inheritance recorded as de novo from that statement about both parents (the paper itself says EOS/sporadic BS, not 'de novo'). Variant printed only as protein shorthand 'R334Q' without 'p.' prefix or transcript; recorded as printed in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; zygosity not stated. Age at BS diagnosis not stated explicitly (BS suspected after the rash at age 10, diagnosis follows genetic testing; age not given), so left not reported; JIA diagnosis at age 2 used as onset of polyarthritis. Age at last evaluation taken from '25-year-old woman', although follow-up continued after tofacitinib start (19+ months), so the age at report may be older. Best-corrected visual acuity 0.5/1 in the left eye is printed as a value only; not called impaired by the paper, so visual impairment left not reported. Table 1 lab values (CRP 0.5 mg/dl vs normal <0.5; ESR 13 vs 1–20) are not called normal or elevated in the text, so 'elevated inflammatory markers' left not reported. Lymphopenia occurred during JAK inhibitor therapy (treatment-related). Literature-review Tables 2 and 3 describe patients with JIA, idiopathic uveitis, VKH or sarcoidosis, none with NOD2 variants or Blau syndrome, so they are out of scope (only the 'Present study' row, the same patient, is Blau). No contradictions found.

span: She was initially treated with acetylsalicylic acid that was discontinued due to drug-induced hepatitis. MTX (3.75 mg/week) and oral methylprednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day) were then started.
She received etanercept, anakinra, and abatacept, but none of them were effective to induce remission of the disease.
she required intensified therapy with ADA (40 mg weekly) and oral MTX up to 20 mg weekly
In addition to methylprednsiolone 6 mg/day, TOFA at a standard dose of 5 mg twice daily was started. ADA and MTX were stopped.
After 2 weeks of ADA, a new off-label treatment with BARI at a standard dose of 4 mg daily was started.
